title: Fijian-style kokoda

ingredients.note: very fresh, skinless, cut in 2 cm cubes

steps: Put the fish in a non-metallic bowl, pour over the lime juice, stir and cover. Chill for 20 to 30 minutes until the fish turns white and firm all the way through.
Drain off most of the lime juice.
Mix in the onion, tomato, chilli and a pinch of salt, then stir in the coconut milk.
Serve cold, within an hour, in bowls or coconut shells.
notes: Use fish that is sold as sashimi-grade and keep it cold. Pregnant people and those with weakened immunity should avoid raw fish.

title: Oven-baked lovo-style chicken, pork and root crops

ingredients.note: peeled and cut in thick pieces
peeled and cut in thick pieces

steps: Heat the oven to 160 C. Season the meat generously with salt and pepper.
Quickly pass the banana leaves over a flame or hot pan to soften them. Overlap them in a large roasting tin, leaving enough overhang to fold over.
Put the pork and chicken in the tin, pour the coconut milk over and fold the leaves over to wrap. Cover the tin tightly with foil.
Cook for 90 minutes. Open, add the cassava and taro, wrap again, and cook for 90 minutes more until the meat is very tender and the roots soft.
Rest for 15 minutes and serve everything together.
notes: Cassava and taro must be fully cooked; both are unpleasant or unsafe raw. This is an oven imitation of a pit cooking method.

title: Taro leaves in coconut milk

ingredients.note: stems removed, leaves washed and torn

steps: Put the onion and garlic in a heavy pot with the coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the taro leaves in handfuls, pushing them under the liquid as they wilt.
Cover and cook on low heat for 40 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, until the leaves are completely tender and the sauce thickened. Season with salt.
notes: Raw taro leaves irritate the mouth and throat, so cook them well. Spinach, silverbeet or fresh taro-leaf substitutes need much less time (about 10 minutes).

title: Baked cassava and coconut pudding

ingredients.note: to line the dish, or baking paper

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C. Line a 20 cm square dish with softened banana leaf or baking paper.
Squeeze the grated cassava in a clean cloth to remove excess liquid. Mix with 250 ml coconut milk, 120 g sugar and the salt.
Spread into the dish, cover with foil and bake for 60 minutes. Uncover and bake for 15 minutes more until set and lightly browned at the edges.
Simmer the remaining coconut milk with 3 tbsp sugar for 8 to 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Cool the pudding a little, cut into squares and serve with the syrup poured over.
notes: Cassava must be thoroughly cooked. Use fresh cassava, not frozen pre-grated, for the best set.

title: Kava drink from powdered root
steps: Put the kava powder in a clean cloth or fine strainer bag and tie it closed.
Submerge the bag in the water in a large bowl, then knead and squeeze it for about 10 minutes until the water turns the colour of muddy milk.
Wring out the bag completely and discard it.
Serve in small cups, traditionally clapping once before drinking and saying 'bula'.
notes: Kava can cause drowsiness. Avoid it with alcohol or medication, and if pregnant or with liver problems. It is a ceremonial drink and best shared with people who know the customs.

title: Yellow split-pea dhal soup
steps: Put the split peas, water and turmeric in a pot and bring to the boil. Skim the foam.
Simmer, partly covered, for 40 to 45 minutes until the peas are soft and falling apart. Whisk or mash to a thin, smooth soup, adding hot water if too thick. Add the salt.
Heat the oil in a small pan. Fry the onion and garlic with the cumin until golden, 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour the sizzling mixture into the dhal, stir once and serve with rice or roti.

title: Goat curry with potatoes
steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and fry the onions for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute, adding a splash of water if it sticks.
Add the goat and brown the pieces for 5 minutes, coating them with the spices. Add the tomato, water and salt.
Cover and simmer gently for 1 hour 15 minutes, until the meat is nearly tender. Add the potatoes and cook for 30 minutes more until soft and the sauce is thick.
Serve with rice or roti.
notes: Lamb shoulder can replace goat; reduce simmering time to about 1 hour 15 minutes in total.

title: Besan ladoo
steps: Melt the ghee in a heavy pan over low heat. Add the gram flour and stir constantly for 15 to 20 minutes until it smells nutty and turns light golden and the mixture loosens.
Take off the heat, stir in the cardamom and let cool for about 10 minutes until warm but not hot.
Mix in the icing sugar thoroughly.
Roll into 12 balls with your palms while the mixture is still warm. If it is too crumbly, add a teaspoon of melted ghee.
Cool completely and store in an airtight container.
notes: Do not rush the roasting; raw flour tastes harsh.

title: Potato and pea samosas
steps: Mix the flour, 4 tbsp oil and salt until crumbly, then add water gradually to form a stiff dough. Knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
For the filling, fry the cumin seeds in 1 tbsp oil for 20 seconds. Add ginger, chilli and turmeric, then the potato and peas. Add garam masala and salt, mix well, cook for 3 to 4 minutes and cool.
Divide the dough into 4 balls. Roll each into a thin oval, cut in half and shape each half into a cone, sealing the seam with a dab of water.
Fill each cone with about 2 tbsp of filling, wet the open edge and press shut.
Heat the frying oil to 165 C. Fry the samosas in batches for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden. Drain and serve hot with chutney.

title: Duruka simmered in coconut milk
steps: Peel off the papery outer husks of the duruka until the pale tender heads are exposed, trim the base, and wash well.
Put the onion, coconut milk and a pinch of salt in a pan and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the duruka and chilli, cover, and cook on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes until tender and the sauce is thick and creamy.
notes: Duruka is hard to find outside Fiji. Fresh asparagus will give a different but pleasant version; cook it for only 5 to 7 minutes.
